summary: Shape an AI vision, prioritise use cases, and build a governed roadmap. Review the course outline and plan your next step.
lede: AI strategy development helps programme leads, product managers, and transformation professionals turn organisational priorities into a practical AI direction. Participants assess readiness using the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 42001 concepts, define outcomes and governance, and rank use cases by value, feasibility, risk, and dependencies. They then sequence initiatives into a roadmap with milestones and progress measures, and prepare an executive decision brief.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who shape AI priorities, assess proposed use cases, or translate executive direction into accountable delivery plans. It is designed for intermediate-level learners with some exposure to AI initiatives or organisational planning.
modules: AI Strategy Mandate and NIST AI RMF
AI Operating Model and OECD Principles
AI Executive Case and Progress Review
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with organisational planning or AI use cases is recommended. You should be able to discuss business priorities and proposed technology initiatives. Programming: Coding is not required. Exercises use planning templates, Excel, and PowerPoint; bring a laptop with access to those applications. No software installation or specialist AI platform is required.
